elements.element: Vendor/Contractor cap set at the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
elements.evidence: "SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE GREATER OF (A) THE fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim AND (B) USD 1,000,000"

elements.element: Cap is mutual (same formulation applies to Customer)
elements.evidence: "COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR ... SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR" — Customer's cap is left lower/narrower than the greater-of formulation, which operates in our favour and is not a deviation to be flagged
"NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES" (untouched)

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for breach of confidentiality obligations
elements.evidence: "do not apply to Excluded Claims ... a party's breach of its confidentiality ... obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for data protection obligations
Uncapped carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights"
"The limitations in paragraph 7(a) do not apply to Excluded Claims. \"Excluded Claims\" means a party's breach ..." — 7(a) contains both parties' caps

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations (Company being the Customer), and all amounts due under this Agreement, are not damages."
Cap is expressed as "THE GREATER OF (A) ... AND (B) USD 1,000,000", which is not a cap equal to 12 months' fees

elements.element: Carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud"

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are operative: the greater-of cap with the exact fee basis and claim anchor plus the USD 1,000,000 floor, the untouched mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the full uncapped carve-out list applying to both parties, and the payment-obligations-are-not-damages statement.
The fallback is separately not met because the cap is a greater-of formulation rather than a cap equal to 12 months' fees; this is irrelevant since the locked target is preferred.
Company's own cap was left at "FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR", so strict mutuality of the greater-of formula is absent, but the narrower Customer-side cap operates in our favour and should not be redlined.

Minimality holds: the first operation changes only the cap amount, preserving the Paragraph 9 exception, and the inserted carve-out sentence is a concise addition for an otherwise absent protection. The parenthetical "(Company being the Customer)" avoids an undefined term, and "all amounts due under this Agreement" is a same-concept clarification favouring us rather than a new exception.
Intent is preserved: paragraph 7(b), the Paragraph 9 indemnity exception and Company's cap remain effective, and no contradiction or dangling mechanic is created.
